added_failures_note: derived from the reviewed run's own arms: baseline_suite lists 9 ids at fe9af3ca and after_suite 11 at the head, and the difference is these two with none fixed. The first is the serial-order fixture at tests/test_one_run_cannot_stop_a_sweep.py:97; the second is recorded in the reviewed manifest's failure_attribution as load-sensitive scaffolding (passes 6/6 in isolation).

findings.text: with promotions running beside the sweep, the fixture's fail_first unlinks r-review-second's pointer during r-review-first's promotion but that run's promotion has already started, so the sweep reports self_promoted ['r-review-second', 'r-review-third'] and this assertion fails; logs/head-arm.log lines 349-380 record exactly that failure for the [True] case, and it fails 2 runs in 3 on its own. The done_when requires no added failure against the base revision, so the node cannot land with this arm red: the fixture must accept the run as promoted-or-vanished or set the width to 1 for that case, which needs a scope extension outside this node's write paths.

PromotionWorkers re-implements a bounded worker pool (semaphore, thread list, outcome map, in-flight set) that the repository already owns twice over: reckon/crew/findings.py:458 runs bounded work through ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=...), and reckon/crew/station.py:66 with :319 starts tracked workers and refuses a duplicate key through _start_thread and _in_flight. Building it on futures and concurrent.futures.wait(timeout=...) would have left one concurrency idiom rather than three, so a later change to any of them has three places to land.

the worker wraps each job in promotion._promotion_host_lease, the same lease promotion.complete already takes at reckon/crew/promotion.py:400. HostLease.claim reattaches on an identical host/pid/job, so the inner claim succeeds, and its release at host_lease.py:151 unlinks the claim file while the outer context still believes it holds the run: the outer claim protects only the pre-promotion phase the docstring names (the gate replay) and its own release is then a no-op returning False, which nothing reads.

after_suite names revision 082b213e8f, but logs/head-arm.log:1 records the head arm as '082b213e8f + uncommitted node changes', so the receipt claims a clean revision for a tree that carried uncommitted changes; the same manifest also leaves measurement_module and measurement_cwd unset although the base arm ran in an extracted tree at /tmp/arms-KoJHeo/base, and those are required for a scratch-tree arm.

the deliverable's first clause is that the sweep records what it finds within a bounded time, but no case in tests/test_a_sweep_never_waits_on_a_promotion.py exercises wait() expiring: every sweep it runs passes wait_seconds 60, longer than the 0.4 s stub, so a change that joined each thread with no timeout, or that dropped outcomes from a promotion still running, would leave all six assertions true.

item_verdicts.diff: read both commits against fe9af3ca from the base: 082b213e8f adds _promotion_settings and PromotionWorkers to reckon/crew/resumption.py, two-phases the review pass in reckon/crew/recovery_review_acceptance.py and adds the six-case test file; 5bc11377cb adds the landing fragment recording both arms and the mutation.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when names four behaviours in tests/test_a_sweep_never_waits_on_a_promotion.py plus a no-added-failure arm pair on a compute partition; the four behaviours pass (logs/head-gate.log 57 passed EXIT=0) and the declared mutation reddens the ordering assertion (logs/negative-control.log EXIT=1), but logs/head-arm.log adds two failure ids against logs/base-arm.log, so the no-added-failure clause is unmet.
item_verdicts.goal: the node goal is that a sweep runs its promotions beside itself up to a configured width; reckon/crew/recovery_review_acceptance.py:896 hands each promotion and acceptance to PromotionWorkers after the pass that dispatches reviews, and reckon/crew/resumption.py:2115 bounds them at the configured width.
item_verdicts.manifest: read the reviewed run's manifest.md: status complete, one code commit plus the evidence commit, baseline_suite and after_suite each carrying revision, literal command, exit_status 1 and completed true with 9 and 11 failure ids, a negative_control_log path whose log ends in a bare EXIT=1, and the added fixture failure recorded under outside_scope.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the declared scope is reckon/crew/resumption.py, reckon/crew/recovery_review_acceptance.py, tests/test_a_sweep_never_waits_on_a_promotion.py and the evidence fragment plus a figures directory; 082b213e8f and 5bc11377cb touch exactly the first three and docs/evidence/fragments/work-flows-to-the-lane/sweep-never-waits-on-a-promotion.html, all inside it.

justifications.durability: the ordering assertion at tests/test_a_sweep_never_waits_on_a_promotion.py:224 reddens when promotions run inline (logs/negative-control.log shows dispatched_at 8716840.09 after first_completion 8716838.84), and the claim and width assertions at :250 and :278 redden if either guard is removed, but no case asserts the wait_seconds bound at reckon/crew/resumption.py:2218.
justifications.evidence: logs/base-arm.log records 6 failed / 483 passed and logs/head-arm.log records 8 failed / 487 passed over the same 60 files on all_debug, so the delta is two added ids where the done_when requires none.
justifications.fit: reckon/crew/resumption.py:2115 follows the module's thread-and-claim idiom and carries no plan label, though reckon/crew/resumption.py:2180 reaches promotion.py's private _promotion_host_lease across the module boundary.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/recovery_review_acceptance.py:896 defers every promotion to the workers handed over at the end of the same pass, so the review a sweep owes is dispatched before any promotion runs.
justifications.reuse: PromotionWorkers at reckon/crew/resumption.py:2115 hand-rolls a bounded worker pool and an in-flight set that reckon/crew/findings.py:458 already expresses with ThreadPoolExecutor and reckon/crew/station.py:66 and :319 already express with _start_thread and _in_flight, while it does reuse the lease at promotion.py:292 and the pass's existing reports/failed/vanished vocabulary.
justifications.scope_discipline: the two commits touch only declare write paths in the reviewed run's manifest.md and no module outside them, adding one class and one config block.
